name: Celestron CPC 800
summary: The main CuzBro observing and imaging platform for lunar, planetary, double-star, cluster, nebula, and galaxy work.
fieldNote: Excellent scale for compact objects. Large targets such as M31, the Veil, and the North America Nebula are a tight fit at native focal length.

name: iPhone 16 Pro
summary: The original CuzBro imaging workflow and the camera behind the first run of lunar and deep-sky mission archive captures.
fieldNote: Still a useful rapid-capture tool even after adding the ASI294MC. The June archive documents how far the smartphone workflow was pushed.

name: ZWO ASI294MC
summary: The current dedicated-camera path for stacked deep-sky imaging and the major step beyond smartphone-only capture.
fieldNote: The first M51 and Fireworks Galaxy session showed a major sensitivity improvement. The next gains should come from longer integration, steadier tracking, and calibration frames.

name: 10 mm Eyepiece
summary: The current high-power eyepiece for compact bright targets after the field has been located and centered.
fieldNote: Use after centering at lower power. Poor seeing can make this view softer rather than more detailed.

name: 25 mm Eyepiece
summary: A middle-ground visual option when the 32 mm view is wider than needed but high power is not yet useful.
fieldNote: Useful as a transition between the 32 mm finder view and the 10 mm high-power view.

name: 32 mm Eyepiece
summary: The default low-power starting eyepiece for locating targets, centering fields, and keeping the widest practical visual view in the current eyepiece set.
fieldNote: SkyMap repeatedly recommends starting here before moving to higher power.

name: Astromania f/6.3 Focal Reducer
summary: A focal reducer used with the CPC 800 to shorten the effective focal length, widen the field of view, and make deep-sky imaging more forgiving.
fieldNote: A major help for deep-sky imaging with the CPC 800. It widens the field and reduces the imaging scale compared with the native f/10 setup.

name: Barlow Lens
summary: An optional magnification step for bright compact targets when seeing supports additional image scale.
fieldNote: Only worth adding when the un-Barlowed image is already steady and sharply focused.

name: Celestron UHC/LPR Filter
summary: The current contrast filter for nebula experiments and comparison captures.
fieldNote: A key planned comparison tool for M27 and the Lagoon Nebula. It is not the default choice for galaxies.

name: Variable Polarizing Filter
summary: Used to reduce glare on bright visual targets when a more comfortable view is useful.
fieldNote: A comfort and glare-control tool rather than a deep-sky contrast filter.

name: Apertura 10x50 RACI Finder
summary: An optical finder for target acquisition and star-field orientation without relying only on the main telescope view.
fieldNote: Particularly useful when verifying the field around small targets before committing to higher magnification.

name: Celestron StarPointer Pro
summary: A zero-magnification reflex finder used for coarse pointing, alignment stars, and quickly getting the CPC 800 onto the right part of the sky.
fieldNote: Best used for getting close quickly. The RACI finder and telescope view handle the precise centering.

name: HBG3 Controller
summary: The current Wi-Fi control bridge used with the CPC 800 and the broader CuzBro telescope-control workflow.
fieldNote: Central to the current control workflow, especially while moving between CPWI-based alignment and mobile observing tools.

name: Celestron Dew Heater Ring
summary: The active dew-control system fitted to the CPC 800 to help keep the corrector plate clear during damp Maine observing sessions.
fieldNote: A key part of the current setup after heavy dew became a real observing problem. The heater ring addresses the corrector plate directly rather than relying on a dew shield.
